sources_read: .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r2/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: 'Quality Checks' row 13 (#12, block 'B - task.toml & run wiring', no_prebuilt_image_shadows_the_agent_dockerfile) and 'Internal Quality Checks' row 13 (same check, wording '...which would skip it entirely'; no additional internal annotation for this row)
evidence: Frozen task.toml [environment] (lines 20-24) contains only build_timeout_sec = 600.0, network_mode = "public", cpus = 2, memory_mb = 4096; tomllib parse confirms 'docker_image' not in [environment] and no other image key anywhere in task.toml. Section is byte-identical in shape to the template task.toml:20-24. The agent Dockerfile (environment/Dockerfile, 26 lines) has active build steps (FROM node:22-bookworm-slim; RUN apt-get install ca-certificates git procps sqlite3; RUN npm install -g express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1; COPY instructions/ and assets/; RUN chmod/git init of /app), so the Dockerfile is the build path and nothing shadows it. No docker-compose file exists in the task tree. Hashes verified: frozen task.toml sha256 15b097b6...bed and Dockerfile 0a75419e...7d1 match manifest.json and the live projects/kittle-matter-chat copies. Adversarial considerations: a broken setup that could pass would be one setting docker_image to a prebuilt image lacking express/better-sqlite3/assets (Dockerfile dead, /assets missing) - not present here; a conforming alternative that could fail (docker_image set with an empty/commented Dockerfile) is not this task's shape and the rule allows it anyway. This is a static configuration check; no runtime measurement is required for it. Whether the Dockerfile actually builds is owned by other rows (15, 11) and is not asserted here.
